notes: Said 'khelt'. No plural. Contant geld = cash; kleingeld = small change.

examples.tl: Ik heb niet genoeg geld bij me.
examples.en: I don't have enough money on me.

notes: Said 'UH-ro' (eu as in French 'peu'). Singular after numbers: vijf euro. € 3,50 is said 'drie vijftig' or 'drie euro vijftig'.

examples.tl: Dat is dan twaalf euro vijftig.
examples.en: That comes to twelve euros fifty.

notes: Said 'prays'. Plural: prijzen. Shelf prices already include tax (btw). Also means 'prize'.

examples.tl: De prijs staat op het kaartje.
examples.en: The price is on the tag.

notes: 'Te duur' = too expensive; duurder = more expensive.

examples.tl: Amsterdam is behoorlijk duur.
examples.en: Amsterdam is pretty expensive.

notes: Said 'khoot-KOHP'. Goedkoper = cheaper.

examples.tl: Heeft u iets goedkopers?
examples.en: Do you have something cheaper?

notes: Ik betaal; past: betaald. Afrekenen = to settle up, pay the bill.

examples.tl: Waar kan ik betalen?
examples.en: Where can I pay?

notes: Cash totals are rounded to the nearest 5 cents: 1 and 2 cent coins are not used.

examples.tl: Ik betaal liever contant.
examples.en: I'd rather pay in cash.

notes: Said as in English. Visa and Mastercard work in most places now, but some small shops and stalls take debit cards only.

examples.tl: Accepteert u creditcards?
examples.en: Do you accept credit cards?

notes: Plural: pinpassen. What locals pay with, contactless, even for one coffee.

examples.tl: Ik ben mijn pinpas vergeten.
examples.en: I forgot my debit card.

notes: Also 'pinautomaat'. The banks' shared ATMs are yellow and branded 'Geldmaat'. Plural: geldautomaten.

examples.tl: De geldautomaat staat naast de supermarkt.
examples.en: The ATM is next to the supermarket.

notes: Often 'bonnetje'. Plural: bonnen. Keep it for exchanges and tax-free forms.

examples.tl: Mag ik de bon, alstublieft?
examples.en: May I have the receipt, please?

notes: Plural: winkels. Winkelen = to go shopping. Most shops close at 6 pm, supermarkets later.

examples.tl: De winkels gaan om tien uur open.
examples.en: The shops open at ten o'clock.

notes: Plural: markten. The Albert Cuypmarkt in Amsterdam runs Monday to Saturday.

examples.tl: Op de markt is de kaas goedkoper.
examples.en: Cheese is cheaper at the market.

notes: Ik koop; past: gekocht. Opposite: verkopen (to sell).

examples.tl: Waar kan ik een simkaart kopen?
examples.en: Where can I buy a SIM card?

notes: Plural: maten. EU sizes: a US men's shoe 10 is about 43-44. S / M / L are used too.

examples.tl: Welke maat heeft u?
examples.en: What size are you?

notes: Plural: tassen. A shopping bag is a 'tasje' and costs a few cents. Rugzak = backpack.

examples.tl: Ik heb mijn eigen tas bij me.
examples.en: I have my own bag with me.

notes: Plural: kortingen. '50% korting' on shop windows. Uitverkoop = clearance sale; aanbieding = special offer.

examples.tl: Krijg ik korting als ik er twee koop?
examples.en: Do I get a discount if I buy two?

notes: Plural: kassa's. Also the ticket desk in a museum. Zelfscankassa = self-checkout.

examples.tl: U kunt bij de kassa betalen.
examples.en: You can pay at the checkout.

notes: The spoken word; signs say 'geopend'. 'Open gaan' = to open (of shops).

examples.tl: Is de supermarkt op zondag open?
examples.en: Is the supermarket open on Sunday?

notes: The spoken word; signs say 'gesloten'. 'Dicht gaan' = to close (of shops).

examples.tl: De bakker is op maandag dicht.
examples.en: The bakery is closed on Mondays.

notes: A deposit of 15 cents on cans and small plastic bottles, 25 on large ones. Supermarket return machines give a refund slip.

examples.tl: Op dit flesje zit statiegeld.
examples.en: There's a deposit on this bottle.

notes: Hoeveel = how much / how many. Equally common: 'Wat kost dit?'

examples.tl: Hoeveel kost dit? — Zeven euro vijftig.
examples.en: How much is this? — Seven euros fifty.

en: Can I pay by credit card?
accept: Can I pay with a credit card?
notes: Worth asking in small shops, at markets and in brown cafés before you order.

examples.tl: Kan ik met creditcard betalen? — Ja hoor, dat kan.
examples.en: Can I pay by credit card? — Sure, you can.

notes: Not a given: plenty of cafés and shops, and all buses, are card-only ('alleen pinnen').

examples.tl: Kan ik contant betalen? — Nee, helaas, alleen met pin.
examples.en: Can I pay cash? — No, sorry, card only.

notes: The answer to 'Kan ik u helpen?' in a shop. Staff will then leave you alone.

examples.tl: Kan ik u helpen? — Nee, dank u, ik kijk alleen even.
examples.en: Can I help you? — No, thank you, I'm just looking.

tl: Heeft u dit in een andere maat?
en: Do you have this in another size?
accept: Do you have this in a different size?
notes: Groter = bigger, kleiner = smaller. 'In een andere kleur' = in another colour.

examples.tl: Heeft u dit in een maat groter?
examples.en: Do you have this one size bigger?

notes: Passen = to try on (and to fit). Paskamer = fitting room.

examples.tl: Mag ik dit passen? — Ja, de paskamers zijn achterin.
examples.en: May I try this on? — Yes, the fitting rooms are at the back.

notes: Present tense does the job of English 'I'll'. 'Deze' = this one (de-word), 'dit' for a het-word.

examples.tl: Ik neem deze. Kan ik pinnen?
examples.en: I'll take this one. Can I pay by card?

notes: 'Te' + adjective = too: te groot (too big), te klein (too small).

examples.tl: Het is mooi, maar het is te duur voor mij.
examples.en: It's nice, but it's too expensive for me.

notes: Asked at almost every till, often shortened to 'Bonnetje?' or 'Bonnetje erbij?'

examples.tl: Wilt u de bon? — Ja, graag.
examples.en: Do you want the receipt? — Yes, please.

notes: Shops may not give plastic bags away free, so you are always asked.

examples.tl: Wilt u een tasje? — Nee, dank u, ik heb een tas.
examples.en: Would you like a bag? — No, thank you, I have a bag.

accept: Where can I take out money?
notes: Geld opnemen = to withdraw money. ATMs are thinner on the ground than they used to be.

examples.tl: Waar kan ik geld opnemen? — Er is een geldautomaat bij het station.
examples.en: Where can I withdraw money? — There's an ATM at the station.

notes: Ruilen = swap for another item. 'Geld terug' (money back) is not always offered. Bring the receipt.

examples.tl: Kan ik dit ruilen? Het is te klein.
examples.en: Can I exchange this? It's too small.

en: Can I get the VAT back?
accept: Can I get a tax refund?
Can I get the tax back?
notes: btw (said 'bay-tay-way') = VAT, 21%. Non-EU residents can reclaim it on larger purchases: ask for a tax-free form, show your passport.

examples.tl: Ik woon buiten de EU. Kan ik de btw terugkrijgen?
examples.en: I live outside the EU. Can I get the VAT back?

tl: Tot hoe laat bent u open?
en: Until what time are you open?
accept_tl: Tot hoe laat zijn jullie open?
notes: 'Tot' = until. To a young shop assistant: 'Tot hoe laat zijn jullie open?'

examples.tl: Tot hoe laat bent u open? — Tot zes uur.
examples.en: Until what time are you open? — Until six.

tl: Kan er nog iets van de prijs af?
en: Can you go down on the price?
accept: Can you do a better price?
Can you give me a discount?
accept_tl: Kan er nog wat van de prijs af?
notes: Only at flea markets (Waterlooplein, IJ-Hallen) and for second-hand things. Haggling in shops is not done.

examples.tl: Twintig euro is wel veel. Kan er nog iets van de prijs af?
examples.en: Twenty euros is a lot. Can you go down on the price?
